requirements: no ambient shadow on ordinary controls
one-pixel lift for solid and outlined actions
directional icon may travel two pixels
never suppressed by hover or error

policies.shape: Use the smallest named radius that preserves the object's role. Controls use twelve pixels. Ordinary cards and panels do not inherit the control radius automatically.
policies.pill: Full rounding is reserved for binary switches, status capsules with short stable content, and genuinely circular controls. It is not the default action shape.
policies.border: Hairlines provide ordinary structure, two-pixel borders mark emphasis or state, and three pixels are reserved for the focus ring. Do not stack borders and shadows to manufacture hierarchy.
policies.depth: Flat is the default. Contact depth exists only during hover, raised depth is reserved for detached temporary surfaces, and overlay depth is reserved for drawers or dialogs. Glow and glass are forbidden.
policies.hierarchy: Use one primary action per decision region, then outlined secondary and text tertiary. Destructive is semantic, not a more exciting primary.
policies.mobile: Use one full-width primary, followed by a quiet secondary link or outline. Preserve a forty-eight-pixel touch target for icon-only actions and never rely on hover.
policies.icons: Use directional icons only when movement, reveal, download, external navigation or continuation becomes clearer. Decorative icons do not enter every button.
policies.accessibility: Keyboard order follows source order. Focus remains visible in every state. Loading retains a name, error retains a message, disabled retains legibility, and forced-colour mode retains boundaries.
policies.motion: Interaction motion is local, fast and interruptible. Reduced motion removes lift and icon travel while preserving colour, border and label feedback.
policies.contentSafety: Labels may wrap only in exceptional high-consequence controls; otherwise controls grow inline or become full-width. Never truncate a destructive or purchase action.
